verdict.rationale: The first-party transport docs describe a WebSocket (wss://) fallback carried by the qmux multiplexer. They also say when it engages: when UDP is blocked or WebTransport is missing, clients race a WebSocket connection and keep whichever wins. The fallback is automatic in every client, the relay enables it with [web.https], and the docs note the TCP head-of-line blocking tradeoff. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that the fallback actually keeps streams alive on UDP-blocked networks.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, a stream survives a network that blocks UDP: the service documents fallback over TCP, TLS, or WebSocket and when it engages

citations.quote: Where UDP is blocked or WebTransport is missing, clients race a WebSocket connection (wss://) and keep whichever wins. A small multiplexer, qmux, carries MoQ streams over the socket.
The fallback is automatic in every client; the relay enables it with [web.https].
